stem: Meera adds vegetable peels and cow dung to a closed pit in her garden in Nagpur. After a few weeks, the waste turns into dark, nutrient-rich manure. Which organisms are mainly responsible for this change?

options.text: Earthworms that eat the waste and convert it into manure on their own
Bacteria and fungi that decompose the waste into simpler substances
Algae growing on the surface that release nutrients from sunlight
Viruses present in the soil that break down the waste

teacher.key_rationale: Decomposition of plant and animal waste into nutrient-rich manure is carried out mainly by soil microorganisms such as bacteria and fungi. Earthworms only assist aeration and mixing; algae are photosynthetic, not decomposers; viruses do not decompose organic waste.
